title: Polymer Science and Engineering
description: An introduction to physical aspects of polymers, including configuration and conformation of polymer chains and characterization techniques; crystallinity, viscoelasticity, mechanical properties, polymer alloys, processing, and application.
prerequisites_raw: ENGR 54 and ( CBE 110 or MSE 165)

title: Surface and Adhesion Science
description: Structure, thermodynamics of, kinetics, and reactions on surfaces. Surface electronic and mechanical properties and characterization of all classes of materials including metals, semiconductors, ceramics, polymers, and soft materials. Adhesion between different materials is also addressed.
prerequisites_raw: ( CBE 110 or MSE 165C ) and ( MSE 141 or MSE 69 )

title: Special Topics in Chemical Engineering
description: Studies in selected areas of Chemical Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering Internship
description: Students majoring in CBE may receive credit for an approved internship, working at a company under the supervision of an industry mentor and a faculty advisor. Enables students to gain valuable experience in a professional setting and enhance their skills.

title: Group Study
description: Group study of selected topics in engineering.

title: Individual Study
description: For undergraduate engineering majors in supervised but independent readings, research, or design. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.

title: Individual Study
description: For undergraduate Engineering majors in supervised but independent reading, research, or design. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in The School of Engineering.

title: Applied Engineering Mathematics I
description: Analytical techniques applied to engineering problems in transport phenomena, process dynamics and control, and thermodynamics.

title: Reaction Engineering
description: Advanced topics in reaction engineering, reactor stability analysis, diffusional effect in heterogeneous catalysis, energy balance, optimization of reactor operation, dispersed in phase reactors.

title: Batteries I: Fundamentals
description: Batteries are electrochemical energy storage devices. Batteries are found in mobile devices as well as transportation or stationary applications. Introduces fundamentals of batteries and organic electrochemistry, operation principles, device limitations, and power densities.

title: Transport Phenomena I
description: Continuum modeling and analysis of heat and mass transfer from an integrated viewpoint. Scaling concepts, relevance of characteristic time- and length-scales, steady- and unsteady-state processes, bounded and unbounded problems, and convective transport, with applications to chemical and biological processes.

title: Advanced Engineering Thermodynamics
description: Introduction to modern thermodynamics and applications, with a focus on aspects relevant to chemical and materials engineering. Mathematical tools; equilibrium and stability; microscope rigorous equations of state; molecular-level thermodynamics of real mixtures; and phase and chemical equilibrium.

title: Electrolyzers: Fundamentals and Applications
description: Hydrogen has potential to decarbonize many sectors, including grid, transportation, chemicals production, and agriculture. Electrolysis is a process where electricity is used to produce hydrogen by splitting water, with no resulting carbon emissions. Several types of electrolyzers are covered.

title: Special Topics in Chemical Engineering
description: Studies in selected areas of Chemical Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Research Methods and Technical Communication
description: Intended for Ph.D. students to develop critical research skills in creating archival papers, intellectual property and technical proposals, and in analysis of the scientific literature.

title: Molecular Biotechnology
description: Engineering and biological principles important in recombinant cell technology. Host/vector selection; plasmid propagation; optimization of cloned gene expression; metabolic engineering; protein secretion; experimental techniques; modeling of recombinant cell systems.

title: Metabolic Engineering and Synthetic Biology
description: Synthesis of chemicals from renewable carbon and energy sources using metabolically engineered biological systems represents one of the most promising solutions to the global problems of energy crisis and climate change.

title: Drug Delivery
description: Introduction to design of drug delivery systems. Includes physicochemical and pharmacokinetic considerations in drug formulations, types of therapeutics, routes of administration, biomaterials, and novel drug delivery systems.

title: Catalysis
description: Establish the microscopic thermodynamics of rate constants and develop quantitative rate laws to model multistep reaction kinetics typical of catalyzed reactions. Common elementary chemical transformations and characteristics of catalytic materials are discussed, citing reactions from industry and current research.

title: Applied Spectroscopy
description: Designed to teach fundamental principles of spectroscopy and their application to photon and electron spectroscopies of the gas and condensed phases. Covers theoretical principles of rotational, vibrational, and electronic spectroscopies. Specific topics include infrared and Raman spectroscopies, Auger, X-ray, etc.

title: Nuclear and Radiochemistry
description: Advanced treatment of nuclear structure, nuclear reactions, and radioactive-decay processes. Introduction to nuclear activation analysis, isotope effects, radiation chemistry, hot-atom chemistry, nuclear age-dating methods, nuclear reactors, and nuclear power.

title: Detection and Measurement of Radiation
description: Basic principles of detection and measurement of ionizing radiation; both theory and practical aspects of measurement techniques for alpha, beta, gamma, and neutron radiation, properties of different detector materials, electronics and data treatments, and analysis.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 233 with a minimum grade of B- or CBE 276 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Advanced Polymer Science and Engineering
description: The synthesis, characterization, microstructure, rheology, and properties of polymer materials. Polymers in solution and in the liquid, crystalline and glassy states. Engineering and processing properties, including viscoelasticity and rheology. Forming and processing methods. Environmental issues.

title: Surface and Adhesion Science
description: Structure, thermodynamics of, kinetics, and reactions on surfaces. Surface electronic and mechanical properties and characterization of all classes of materials including metals, semiconductors, ceramics, polymers, and soft materials. Adhesion between different materials is also addressed.

title: Seminars in Engineering
description: Seminars scheduled each year by individual faculty in major field of interest.

title: Special Topics in Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering
description: Studies in selected areas of Master of Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Master of Science Thesis Research
description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation for the thesis required for the M.S. degree.

title: Doctor of Philosophy Dissertation Research
description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation for the dissertation required for the Ph.D. degree.

title: Seminars in Engineering
description: Presentation of advanced topics and reports of current research efforts in chemical engineering.

title: Introduction to Chicano/Latino Studies I
description: An introduction to the study of the historical foundations of the Chicano/Latino experience. Addresses such topics as empire, migration, immigrant settlement, economic integration, race, gender, and the formation of group identities.

title: Introduction to Chicano/Latino Studies II
description: Provides an introduction to the arts, literature, and culture of Chicano/Latino communities. Analyzes representations of and cultural production in Chicano/Latino communities through such media as folklore, literature, art, film, architecture, dance theatre, performance, music, poetry, mass media, and language.

title: Introduction to Chicano/Latino Studies III
description: Examines contemporary public policy issues in Chicano/Latino communities. Each offering addresses at least three of the following themes: migration, immigrant incorporation, identity construction, language policy, health policy, politics, sexuality, gender, labor, class, and education.

title: Introduction to Race and Ethnicity in Political Science
description: Examines major theories that attempt to explain the roles of race and ethnicity in U.S. politics.

title: Ethnic and Immigrant America
description: Focusing on Asian, Latino, and Black immigrant groups, examines the second generation's experience of straddling two cultures and growing up American. Covers topics such as assimilation, bilingualism, race relations, education, bicultural conflicts, interracial marriage, and multiracial identities.

title: Research in the Latino Community
description: Students engage in firsthand research in the local Orange County environment. Students identify a research problem, conduct a literature review, develop questions and/or hypotheses, appropriate methods, and write a proposal.
prerequisites_raw: CHC/LAT 61 or CHC/LAT 62 or CHC/LAT 63 . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement. Recommended: Two courses from CHC/LAT 110 -189

title: Chicano/Latino Research Seminar
description: Taught as a writing and research seminar in Chicano/Latino Studies. Student develops own project; engages in peer editing; drafts, writes, and presents paper at Spring research conference. Prior course work in Chicano/Latino Studies helpful, i.e., CHC/LAT 61 , 62 , 63 .
prerequisites_raw: CHC/LAT 101 . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Topics in Chicano Literature and Culture
description: Studies in selected areas of Chicano/Latino Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter. Taught in English.

title: Afro-Latin American Music
description: Musical culture of Afro-Latin American peoples, emphasizing Spanish-speaking Caribbean. Topics include background in West Africa, the persistence of traditions in the Caribbean, the commercial music of the 20th century, the connections between musical culture, religion, and the economy.

title: Anthropology of Food
description: Examines how food communicates ideas about ethnocentrism, disgust, privilege, gender, race, labor, social identities and hierarchies, globalization, power, and the "Western diet" and its health consequences.

title: Peoples and Cultures of Latin America
description: Surveys the prehistory of Latin America and its indigenous cultures, emphasizing the impact of colonial rule, capitalism, and 20th-century transformations. Emphasis on communities from several countries. In some years, emphasis on comparisons between the Latin American and Caribbean experiences.

title: Latina/Latino Pop: Latina/Latino Popular Culture
description: With a focus on the politics of language and space/place, prepares students to critically analyze sites of Latina/Latino popular culture including: music, film, performance, sports, media, and varied subcultures.

title: Immigrant Emotionality
description: Explores the emotional universe created by the Latin American immigrant experience, and guides students in the creation of a literary work based on an investigation into, or reflection on that experience.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Latinx Performance
description: Explores Latinx cultural history from the 19th century to the present through the lens of theater and performance. Analyzes the Latinx experience as seen in plays, films, social media, visual culture, music, and archival sources.

title: Special Topics in Literature, Arts, Media, Culture
description: Studies in selected areas of Chicano/Latino Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Histories of Chicana/o/x and Latina/o/x Struggles for Civil Rights, 1960-1980
description: Provides students with an opportunity to learn more about the historical, political, and social underpinnings that oriented the civil rights struggles of mid-to-late 20th-century Chicana/o/x and Latina/o/x activists.

title: Black Latinidades
description: Questions the parameters of Latinidad by centering the origins and development of African descent communities in the Americas through a multidisciplinary, transnational, and diasporic approach to the study of Afro-Latinidad.

title: Chicana/Chicano History: Twentieth Century
description: Examines social history of the Southwest with emphasis on Mexican-origin people. Discusses major questions, theory and research methods pertinent to Chicana/Chicano history. Themes explored include: immigration, xenophobia, class struggle, leadership, generational cohorts, unionization, education, barrioization, ethnicity, patriarchy, sexuality.

title: Intergenerational Latina/o/x Histories
description: Students learn from institutional and intergenerational histories and the scholarship of the Chicano/Latino Studies faculty emeriti who founded the Department and contributed to its scholarly presence and impact.

title: U.S. Latino Literature and Cultures
description: Focuses on aspects of literature, art, cultural production, and history of the multifaceted Latino cultures that have developed within the United States. Focuses on one group, such as Caribbean Americans, Chicanos, Central Americans, or a comparative perspective of several groups.

title: Latinas in the Twentieth Century U.S
description: Latinas in the U.S. from 1900 to present, offering a diversity of their cultures, regional histories, sexualities, generations, and classes.

title: Special Topics in Chicano/Latino History
description: Studies in selected areas of Chicano/Latino History. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Latinx Racial Formations
description: Students explore the meanings attributed to Latina/o/x racial identities over time; the political, economic, and social structures that have shaped those identities; and their impact on Latinx self-concepts, interpersonal/intra-community relations, and life chances.

title: Comparative Minority Politics
description: Examines the political experiences of Blacks, Latinos, and Asian Americans in the United States from roughly 1950 to the present. Focuses on how each group has pursued political empowerment via both conventional political channels and social movements.

title: Racial and Ethnic Relations in the United States
description: Examines central questions and issues in the field of race and ethnicity; the emergence, maintenance, and consequences of the ethnic and racial stratification system in the United States; the future of racial and ethnic relations; and relevant public policy issues.

title: Racial and Ethnic Relations in the United States
description: Examines central questions and issues in the field of race and ethnicity; the emergence, maintenance, and consequences of the ethnic and racial stratification system in the United States; the future of racial and ethnic relations; and relevant public policy issues.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: U.S. Intervention in Latin America
description: Explores political, economic, social, and cultural ties that bind Latin America to the United States. Focuses on U.S. intervention and Latin American response from early nineteenth century to present day. Case studies include Mexico, Guatemala, Cuba, Chile, and Central America.

title: Sex and Conquest in Latin America
description: Competing ideas of masculinity and femininity, sexual violence, sexual identities, and gendered hierarchies informed how the Spanish engaged in military and religious domination of Mexican and Andean communities, as well as the forms of native resistance throughout colonial Latin America.

title: Latinos in U.S. Politics
description: Comparing the political issues facing Latino groups by examining their migration histories, voting behavior, nonelectoral participation, and policy issues. Latino issues are examined on the national, state, and local levels, including formal representation, immigration, affirmative action, and language policy.

title: Revolution in Latin America
description: Presents a comparative analysis of the causes, development, and consequences of selected revolutionary movements, focusing on outbreaks in Mexico, Bolivia, Cuba, Chile, Nicaragua, and Grenada. Explores topics of state formation, economic nationalism, social justice, ethnicity, and role of international affairs.

title: Race, Ethnicity, and Social Control
description: Provides a historical and sociological survey of racial and ethnic group relations in contexts of crime control, emphasizing the roles of racial ideology, structural racism, and social movements in shaping these dynamic relations, and their significance to American liberal democracy.

title: Community, Social Justice, and Health Equity Research for Action
description: Focuses on community as a unit of identity, community, well-being, and social justice perspectives and initiatives to promote community health. Addresses community change and improvements in community well-being, with a focus on health equity research for action.
prerequisites_raw: PUBHLTH 1 or PUBHLTH 2 or CHC/LAT 61 or CHC/LAT 62 or CHC/LAT 63

title: Latino Metropolis
description: Explores the processes of Latino urbanization in the United States and the spatialization of Latino identities, particularly in the context of Southern California with selected comparisons drawing from other cities.

title: Critical Latinx Indigeneities
description: Introduces students to the emerging field of Critical Latinx Indigeneities. This interdisciplinary field brings together Chicanx/Latinx studies, Indigenous studies, and Latin American studies to examine how Latinidad obfuscates the experiences of Indigenous Latinx peoples in the U.S.

title: Chicano/Latinos and Labor
description: Explores theories that explain the occupational pathways and workplace experiences of Latinos in various work sectors. Investigates jobs such as migrant labor, child street vendors, Latina/Latino professionals, and Latinos migrating to the U.S. South that work in poultry processing plants.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Cuban Society and Revolution
description: Explores the causes, development, and legacy of the 1959 Revolution. Themes include economic dependency, democracy, race, gender, culture, and the always volatile relations between Cuba and the United States.

title: Feminisms of Color
description: Surveys the development of Chicana feminist thought and practice. Focuses on historical contemporary writings by and about Chicana feminists. Draws from interdisciplinary scholarship in order to survey the diversity of Chicana feminisms.

title: Gender and Ethnicity: Chicana/Latina Feminisms in the US
description: Focuses on the Latina Feminist Group and testimonios to examine the historical development of Chicana/Latinx feminist thought and practice. Draws from interdisciplinary scholarship to survey the diversity of contemporary Chicana/Latinx feminisms through an intersectionality lens.

title: Special Topics in Society, Labor, Politics, Law, Gender, Race, Ethnicity
description: Studies in selected areas of Chicano/Latino Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Transnational Migration
description: Examines the movement of people across national borders, governmentality and the role of state practices to control populations, and issues of citizenship, belonging, and identity. Examples are drawn from the United States, Europe, Latin America, Asia, and Africa.

title: Transnational Central America
description: Offers an overview of the history of Central America and its diasporas, as well as the struggles, accomplishments, and activism, art and cultural expressions of Central Americans in the United States.

title: Race in the City: Past, Present, and Future
description: Students examine the historical, social, political, and economic factors that contributed to the construction of the American urban context, one that is poverty concentrated and racially/ethnically segregated. Students also critically assess the consequence of growing up in America's urban neighborhoods.

title: U.S. Immigration Policy
description: Examines selected immigration policy debates since the nineteenth century, rationale and consequences of immigration law since 1965, problems of administration, implementation and enforcement, impact of immigration policy on foreign relations, and contemporary debate regarding the future of U.S. policy.

title: Undocumented Immigrant Experiences
description: Examines the experiences of undocumented immigrants and the policies that structure their educational, economic, social, and political participation.

title: Chicano/Latino Social Psychology
description: Examines theories, research, and major issues of relevance to understanding social psychological processes in Chicano/Latino populations. Topics include social development, cultural orientations, gender and sexuality, close relationships, happiness and well-being, stereotyping, prejudice and discrimination, and mental and physical health.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Special Topics in Globalization, Transnationalism, Immigration, U.S.-Mexico Border
description: Studies in selected areas of Chicano/Latino Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Chicano/Latino Families
description: Introduction to the research, literature, and issues surrounding the topic of Chicano/Latino families including cultural history, contemporary issues, organization of family, traditions, lifestyles, values, beliefs, generational differences, gender issues, ethnic identity, evolution of demographic patterns, current economic and political standings.

title: Latinas and Chronic Illness: Cultural and Psychological Perspectives
description: Explores chronic illness in Latina communities through a qualitative lens, focusing on cultural values, healthcare access, and systemic barriers. Students design and conduct a group-based study to better understand lived experiences and health inequities.

title: Latina Reproductive Health
description: Gives an overview of active areas of research on the psychological, social, and cultural factors that influence Latina reproductive health. Critically examines selected topics in reproductive health not merely as biological processes, but as psychological events.

title: Race, Gender, and Science
description: Perfect for pre-health, science, and social science majors wanting to appreciate how science and society interact. Race and gender as biological and socio-cultural constructs are examined. Questions explored: What is disease? What is science? What are social and biological differences?

title: Health and the Latino Paradox
description: Examines research and theories concerning the physical and mental health of U.S. Latino populations. Contemporary accounts, health care implications, and new directions for understanding sources of risks and resilience for health in Latino populations are evaluated and discussed.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Medical Anthropology
description: Introduces students to cross-cultural perspectives and critical theories in anthropological studies of medicine. Special attention is given to diverse ways of understanding bodies, illnesses, and therapeutic practices in our changing world.

title: Special Topics in Health, Medicine, and Psychosocial Dynamics
description: Studies in selected areas of Chicano/Latino Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Chicane/Latine Education
description: Provides a historical and empirical overview of educational issues affecting diverse Latine low-income, immigrant, and U.S. born student populations enrolled in American schools. Examines policies and issues such as DACA, generation, culture, racism, and gender on educational mobility.

title: Multicultural Education in K-12 Schools
description: Provides a theoretical and empirical overview of educational issues affecting low-income immigrant and U.S. born minority student populations in an increasingly diverse and changing society.

title: Special Topics in Educational Policy and Issues
description: Studies in selected areas of Chicano/Latino Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Honors Research Preparation
description: Students write a proposal describing their research question, the relevant background literature, and the method of data collection and analysis. Field work for the project may begin this quarter.

title: Honors Field Research
description: Students begin or continue their research for their senior honors thesis.
prerequisites_raw: CHC/LAT H190A

title: Honors Thesis
description: Student drafts a senior honor thesis (typically) with the following sections: problem statement, literature review, description of the methods, results, and conclusions.
prerequisites_raw: CHC/LAT H190A and CHC/LAT H190B

title: Honors Thesis
description: Student drafts a senior honor thesis (typically) with the following sections: problem statement, literature review, description of the methods, results, and conclusions.
prerequisites_raw: CHC/LAT H190A and CHC/LAT H190B . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Directed Group Study
description: Directed study with Chicano/Latino faculty.

title: Independent Study
description: Independent research with Chicano/Latino faculty.

title: Theoretical Issues in Chicano/Latino Research
description: Introduction to theoretical issues in the scholarship in Chicano/Latino Studies. Theories from social sciences, humanities, critical theory. Topics: immigration, identity, gender and sexuality, globalization, transnationalism, social, political, and economic integration, race theory, labor market participation, social history, cultural productions.

title: Cultural and Historial Precedents for Latinos and Medical Care
description: Introduction to the history of Latinos, focusing on relevant pre-Columbian, colonial, and modern social and cultural developments, including issues of race, gender, sexuality, religious beliefs, and health beliefs and practices.

title: Cultural and Historical Precedents for Latinos and Medical Care
description: Introduction to the history of Latinos, focusing on relevant pre-Columbian, colonial, and modern social and cultural developments, including issues of race, gender, sexuality, religious beliefs, and health beliefs and practices.
prerequisites_raw: CHC/LAT 210A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Latinos/Latinas and Medical Care: Contemporary Issues
description: Introduction to medical anthropological and social science perspectives on Latinos/Latinas in relation to a number of health and medically-related issues, i.e., immigration, gender, reproduction, culture, social structure, political economy, sexuality, utilization of medical services, and health beliefs.

title: Latinos/Latinas and Medical Care: Contemporary Issues
description: Introduction to medical anthropological and social science perspectives on Latinos/Latinas in relation to a number of health and medically-related issues, i.e., immigration, gender, reproduction, culture, social structure, political economy, sexuality, utilization of medical services, and health beliefs.
prerequisites_raw: CHC/LAT 211A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Transnational Migration
description: Examines borders and boundaries as material and semiotic constructs. Drawing upon an array of literatures, but loosely situated in U.S. geo/biopolitics, explores transformative troublings of places, spaces, borders, and bodies of all sorts.

title: Ethnography
description: Explores the theory and practice of ethnography with a focus on anthropology, the discipline most associated with ethnography. Students are exposed to the theoretical underpinnings of ethnographic work, traditional and innovative practices, and sample ethnographies.

title: Ethnic America
description: Examines critically the meaning and measurement of ethnicity, race, and nation in sociological theory and research. Theories of ethnicity are explored, along with empirical studies of the construction of ethnic and pan-ethnic identities in historical and contemporary contexts.

title: Immigrant America
description: The study of the causes and consequences of international migration has become one of the most vital fields of sociological theory and research. Examines principal theoretical perspectives and empirical research on contemporary immigration flows and the processes of incorporation.

title: Crimmigration
description: Examines the criminalization of immigration, with an emphasis on U.S. enforcement procedures and outcomes. Analyzes the devolution of federal immigration law to local authorities, the rise in immigrant detention and deportation, and the militarization of the U.S.-Mexico border.

title: Models of Practice and Intervention at the Community Level
description: Examines and critiques current models, frameworks, theories for understanding social and behavioral factors that are central to community health, and to the development, implementation, evaluation of interventions that encompass behavioral change at the group, organization, community, societal, policy, or multilevel.
prerequisites_raw: CHC/LAT 200A with a minimum grade of B- or PUBHLTH 246 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Special Topics in Chicano/Latino Studies
description: Current research in Chicano/Latino Studies.

title: Dissertation Research
description: Dissertation research with Chicano/Latino faculty.

title: General Chemistry
description: General chemistry with applications to life sciences, physical sciences, and engineering. Atomic structure; general properties of the elements; covalent, ionic, and metallic bonding; mass relationships.
prerequisites_raw: MATH 5A or MATH 2A or PHYSICS 7C or CHEM 1X or CHEM 1P with a minimum grade of C- or SAT Mathematics with a minimum score of 600 or ACT Mathematics with a minimum score of 27 or SAT Subject Chemistry with a minimum score of 700 or AP Chemistry with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 3. Placement via a passing score on the UCI placement exam or a passing score on the ALEKS placement exam is also accepted

title: General Chemistry
description: General chemistry with applications to life sciences, physical sciences, and engineering. Properties of gases, liquids, solids; intermolecular forces; changes of state; properties of solutions; stoichiometry; thermochemistry; and thermodynamics.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 1A with a minimum grade of C- or ENGR 1A with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM H2A with a minimum grade of C- or AP Chemistry with a minimum score of 4 or CHEM M2A with a minimum grade of C-

title: General Chemistry
description: General chemistry with applications to life sciences, physical sciences, and engineering. Equilibria, aqueous acid-base equilibria, solubility equilibria, oxidation reduction reactions, electrochemistry; kinetics; special topics.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 1B with a minimum grade of C-

title: General Chemistry Laboratory
description: Training and experience in basic laboratory techniques. Chemical practice and principles illustrated through experiments related to lecture topics of CHEM 1A -B-C. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 1B with a minimum grade of C- or ENGR 1A with a minimum grade of C-

title: General Chemistry Laboratory
description: Training and experience in basic laboratory techniques. Chemical practice and principles illustrated through experiments related to lecture topics in CHEM 1A -B-C. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ( CHEM 1C with a minimum grade of C- and CHEM 1LC with a minimum grade of C-) or CHEM 1LE with a minimum grade of C-

title: Preparation for General Chemistry
description: Units of measurement, dimensional analysis, significant figures; elementary concepts of volume, mass, force, pressure, energy, density, temperature, heat, work; fundamentals of atomic and molecular structure; the mole concept, stoichiometry; properties of the states of matter; gas laws; solutions concentrations.

title: General Chemistry Plus
description: Units of chemical measurements, dimensional analysis, significant figures; elementary physicochemical concepts; fundamentals of atomic and molecular structure; molar amounts and stoichiometry; properties of the states of matter; solutions concentrations.
prerequisites_raw: Students who meet the requirements for taking Chem 1A through their SAT, ACT, or AP test scores are not eligible for enrollment in Chem 1X. Specifically, the students must have ALL of the following advisory prerequisites (the inverse of the Chem 1A prerequisites): S02<600 (score below 600 on the SAT Mathematics Reasoning test) A02<27 (score below 27 on the ACT Mathematics test) Z43<700 (score below 700 on the SAT Chemistry subject exam) AP25<3 (score below 3 on the AP Chemistry exam) AP66<3 (score below 3 on the AP Calculus AB Exam) AP68<3 (score below 3 on the AP Calculus BC Exam) Students who meet Chem 1A eligibility through ALEKS-based training are permitted to enroll in Chem 1X. Chem 1X is open to interested BioEASE students

title: Majors General Chemistry Lecture
description: Covers the same material as CHEM 1A but in greater depth. Additional topics are included as time permits.
prerequisites_raw: MATH 5A or MATH 2A or PHYSICS 7C or CHEM 1X or CHEM 1P with a minimum grade of C- or SAT Mathematics with a minimum score of 600 or ACT Mathematics with a minimum score of 27 or SAT Subject Chemistry with a minimum score of 700 or AP Chemistry with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 3. Placement via a passing score on the ALEKS placement exam is also accepted

title: Majors General Chemistry Lecture
description: Covers the same material as CHEM 1B but in greater depth. Additional topics will also be included as time permits.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM M2A with a minimum grade of C- and CHEM M2LA with a minimum grade of C-

title: Majors General Chemistry Lecture
description: Covers the same material as CHEM 1C but in greater depth. Additional topics are also included as time permits.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM M2B with a minimum grade of C- and CHEM M2LB with a minimum grade of C-

title: Majors General Chemistry Laboratory
description: Training and experience in basic laboratory techniques through experiments related to lecture topics in CHEM 1A - CHEM 1B -CHEM M3C. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: CHEM M2A (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C-. High school chemistry

title: Majors General Chemistry Laboratory
description: Training and experience in basic laboratory techniques through experiments related to lecture topics in CHEM 1A - CHEM 1B -CHEM M3C. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ( CHEM 1B with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM H2B with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM M2B with a minimum grade of C-) and ( CHEM M2A with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM H2A with a minimum grade of C-) and ( CHEM M2LA with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM H2LA with a minimum grade of C-)

title: Majors Quantitative Analytical Chemistry Laboratory
description: Foundational principles of analytical chemistry and experimental methods for quantitative analysis of real samples. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ( CHEM 1B with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM H2B with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM M2B with a minimum grade of C-) and ( CHEM M2LB with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM H2LB with a minimum grade of C-)

title: Scientific Mathematical and Computing Skills
description: Introduces students to mathematical skills, including complex numbers, linear algebra, differential equations, multivariable calculus, infinite series, Fourier series, and integral transforms; and computing skills, including plotting, data analysis (statistics and curve fitting), linear algebra, symbolic mathematics, and spectral analysis.
prerequisites_raw: ( CHEM 1C (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM H2C (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM M3C (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM M2C (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C-) and MATH 2D (may be taken concurrently)

title: New Chemistry Student Seminar
description: Seminar for students who recently joined the chemistry major. Addresses available tracks in the major, research opportunities in the chemistry department, careers in chemistry, and relevant programs and resources for students.

title: Sense and Sensibility in Science
description: Gives an overview of scientific methods and heuristics through group exercises and discussion. Discusses the benefits and limitations of applying rational scientific approaches to real-world examples from philosophy, cognitive and social psychology, game theory, economics, political science, law, and negotiation.

title: Organic Chemistry
description: Fundamental concepts relating to carbon compounds with emphasis on structural theory and the nature of chemical bonding, stereochemistry, reaction mechanisms, and stereoscopic, physical, and chemical properties of the principal classes of carbon compounds.
prerequisites_raw: ( CHEM 1C with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM H2C with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM M2C with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM M3C with a minimum grade of C-) and ( CHEM 1LD with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM H2LB with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM M2LB with a minimum grade of C-)

title: Organic Chemistry
description: Fundamental concepts relating to carbon compounds with emphasis on structural theory and the nature of chemical bonding, stereochemistry, reaction mechanisms, and stereoscopic, physical, and chemical properties of the principal classes of carbon compounds.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 51A with a minimum grade of C- and ( CHEM 1LD with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM M52LA with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM H52LA with a minimum grade of C-)

prerequisites_raw: CHEM 51B with a minimum grade of C- and ( CHEM 51LB with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM M52LB with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM H52LB with a minimum grade of C-)

description: Modern techniques of organic chemistry, using selected experiments to illustrate topics introduced in CHEM 51A - CHEM 51B - CHEM 51C . Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 51A with a minimum grade of C- and ( CHEM 1LD with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM H2LB with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM M2LB with a minimum grade of C-)

description: Modern techniques of organic chemistry, using selected experiments to illustrate topics introduced in CHEM 51A -B-C. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 51B with a minimum grade of C- and CHEM 51LB with a minimum grade of C-

prerequisites_raw: CHEM 51C with a minimum grade of C- and CHEM 51LC with a minimum grade of C-

description: Modern techniques of organic chemistry, using selected experiments to illustrate topics introduced in CHEM 51A -B-C. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ( CHEM 1C with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM H2C with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM M2C with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM M3C with a minimum grade of C-) and (CHEM H2LB with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM M2LB with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM 1LD with a minimum grade of C-)

title: Majors Organic Chemistry Laboratory
description: Modern techniques of organic chemistry, using selected experiments to illustrate topics introduced in CHEM 51A -B-C. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 51A with a minimum grade of C- and CHEM M52LA with a minimum grade of C-

title: Majors Organic Chemistry Laboratory
description: Modern techniques of organic chemistry, using selected experiments to illustrate topics introduced in CHEM 51A -B-C. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 51B with a minimum grade of C- and ( CHEM M52LB with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM H52LB with a minimum grade of C-)

title: The Idiom and Practice of Science
description: A series of fundamental and applied problems in the chemical sciences are addressed. Topics may include the periodic table, electronic structure of atoms, chemical bonding, molecular structure, thermodynamics, and kinetics, with applications to energy and the environment, and/or biochemistry.

title: Special Topics in Chemistry
description: Devoted to current topics in the advanced fields of chemical sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: ( CHEM 51C or CHEM H52C) and (CHEM M3C or CHEM M2C or CHEM 1C or CHEM H2C)

title: Laboratory Safety for Chemists
description: Provide students with the fundamentals of safety involved in chemical laboratory work.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 51C (may be taken concurrently)

title: Writing in Chemical Sciences
description: Students receive guidance on preparing research papers, proposals, reports, and other forms of scientific writing in chemistry-related fields, on effectively searching for and using chemical information, and on communicating data in poster and platform presentations.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Inorganic Chemistry
description: Introduction to modern inorganic chemistry. Principles of structure, bonding, and chemical reactivity with application to compounds of the main group and transition elements, including organometallic chemistry.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 51C or CHEM H52C

title: Inorganic Chemistry Laboratory
description: Modern techniques of inorganic and organometallic chemistry, including experience with glove box, Schlenk line, and vacuum line methods. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 107 and CHEM 100S

title: Advanced Organic Chemistry
description: Rapid-paced comprehensive treatment of organic chemistry. Focuses on molecular structure, reactivity, stability, scope and mechanisms of organic reactions. Topics include: structure and bonding; theoretical organic chemistry; acidity and basicity; reactive intermediates; pericyclic reactions; stereochemistry; organic synthesis; natural products; organic photochemistry.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 51C

title: Inorganic Chemistry II
description: Advanced treatment of selected fundamental topics in inorganic chemistry, building on material presented in Chemistry 107. Molecular symmetry with applications to electronic structure and spectroscopy. Reaction kinetics and mechanisms; inorganic synthesis and catalysis; bioinorganic chemistry.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 107

title: Introduction to Chemical Biology
description: Introduction to the basic principles of chemical biology: structures and reactivity; chemical mechanisms of enzyme catalysis; chemistry of signalling, biosynthesis, and metabolic pathways.
prerequisites_raw: ( CHEM 51C or CHEM H52C)

title: Introduction to Chemical Biology Laboratory Techniques
description: Introduction to the basic laboratory techniques of chemical biology: electrophoresis, plasmid preparation, PCR, protein expression, isolation, and kinetics. Materials Fee

title: Chemical Thermodynamics, Kinetics, and Dynamics
description: Energy, entropy, and the thermodynamic potentials. Chemical equilibrium. Chemical kinetics.
prerequisites_raw: MATH 2D and ( PHYSICS 7D or PHYSICS 7E ) and ( CHEM 5 or ( MATH 3A and ( EECS 10 or EECS 12 or ENGRMAE 10 or I&C SCI 31 )) )

title: Quantum Principles, Spectroscopy, and Bonding
description: Principles of quantum chemistry with applications to the elements of atomic structure, energy levels, and spectroscopy.
prerequisites_raw: ( CHEM 132A with a minimum grade of C- or CBE 40C ) and ( PHYSICS 7D or PHYSICS 7E )

title: Molecular Structure and Elementary Statistical Mechanics
description: Principles of quantum mechanics with applications to molecular spectroscopy and structure determination, and chemical bonding in simple molecules. Elements of statistical mechanics.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 132B

title: Nuclear and Radiochemistry
description: Advanced treatment of nuclear structure, nuclear reactions, and radioactive-decay processes. Introduction to nuclear activation analysis, isotope effects, radiation chemistry, hot-atom chemistry, nuclear age-dating methods, nuclear reactors, and nuclear power.
prerequisites_raw: (CHEM M3C or CHEM 1C or CHEM H2C or CHEM M2C ) and MATH 2D

title: Nuclear and Radiochemistry Laboratory
description: Practical aspects of production, separation, safe handling, detection, and measurement of radioactive isotopes. Experiments use the UCI nuclear reactor and emphasize uses of radioisotopes in chemistry, engineering, biology, and medicine. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 133 (may be taken concurrently)

title: Introduction to Computational Organic Chemistry
description: An introduction to the use of computational chemistry to investigate reaction mechanisms, to calculate structures, and to predict properties of molecules. Students have the opportunity to perform calculations employing computational methods which are widely used in various fields of chemistry. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 51C

title: Environmental Chemistry
description: Processes that control the fate of chemicals in the environment. Chemistry of the atmosphere, hydrosphere, and soils, especially as it pertains to pollutants.
prerequisites_raw: ( CHEM 51C or CHEM H52C) and ( MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4)

title: Gas-Phase Atmospheric Chemistry
description: Sources, chemistry, sinks, and measurements of key atmospheric gaseous species. Chemistry of photochemical oxidant formation, transformation of key inorganic and organic trace gases, and stratospheric ozone cycling. Applications of atmospheric chemistry models to control strategies.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 132A and CHEM 132B and CHEM 132C

title: Multi-Phase Atmospheric Chemistry
description: Chemical and physical processes leading to the production, aging, and removal of atmospheric particles. Multi-phase processes involving gases, particles, water droplets, and environmental surfaces. Approaches for modeling these processes with applications to control strategies.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 145A

title: Computational Chemistry
description: Basic concepts, methods, and techniques in computational chemistry: density functional and wavefunction theory, molecular property calculations, analysis tools, potential energy surfaces, vibrational effects, molecular dynamics simulations.
prerequisites_raw: MATH 3A and ( CHEM 132A or PHYSICS 113A )

title: Computational Chemistry Laboratory
description: Introduction to the practice of modern computational chemistry through a series of advanced computational experiments.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 150 and ( CHEM 5 or PHYSICS 50 or EECS 12 )

title: Advanced Analytical Chemistry
description: In-depth treatment of modern instrumental methods for quantitative analysis of real samples and basic principles of instrument design. Laboratory experiments using spectroscopic, chromatographic, mass spectrometric, and other instrumental methods. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ( CHEM 1C or CHEM M3C or CHEM H2C or CHEM M2C ) and ( CHEM M3LC or CHEM H2LC)

title: Physical Chemistry Laboratory
description: Introduction to the modern experimental approaches and software tools used in spectroscopy, kinetics, electrochemistry, and other physical chemistry experiments. Basics of interfacing with instruments using LabView. Materials Fee

title: Advanced Laboratory in Chemistry and Synthesis of Materials
description: Modern synthesis and characterization of organic and inorganic materials including polymers, nanomaterials, and biomaterials. State-of-the-art characterization techniques include gel permeation chromatography, dynamic light scattering, thermal analysis, mechanical analysis, electron and scanning probe microscopy, X-ray diffraction, and porosimetry. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ( CHEM 51C or CHEM H52C) and ( CHEM 51LC or CHEM H52LC or CHEM M52LC ) and (CHEM 131A or CHEM 132B or PHRMSCI 171 )

title: Organic Synthesis Laboratory
description: Modern experimental techniques in organic synthesis including experience with thin-layer chromatography, liquid chromatography, and gas chromatography. Modern methods of structure elucidation including FT NMR are employed in the characterization of products. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 51C and CHEM 100S and ( CHEM 51LC or CHEM H52LC or CHEM M52LC )

title: Medicinal Chemistry
description: Surveys drug target classes; lead identification and optimization; pharmacokinetics; discovery strategies including natural product chemistry, encoded combinatorial libraries, molecular modeling, and high-throughput screening; case studies in antiviral, antibacterial, and anticancer drug discovery and development.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 51A and CHEM 51B and CHEM 51C and ( BIO SCI 98 or CHEM 128 ). Recommended: BIO SCI 99

title: Medicinal Chemistry Laboratory
description: Introduction to high-throughput experimentation for identifying bioactive compounds. Techniques include microplate assay setup, IC50 determination, quantitative assay development, library screening, and structure-activity analysis. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 51A and CHEM 51B and CHEM 51C and ( BIO SCI 98 or CHEM 128 )

title: Undergraduate Research
description: Research for credit arranged with a faculty member to sponsor and supervise work. Student time commitment of 10 to 15 hours per week is expected, and a written research report is required at the end of each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 100S (may be taken concurrently)

title: Senior Thesis in Chemistry
description: Students receive guidance on preparing research papers, proposals, reports, and other forms of scientific writing in chemistry-related fields; on effectively searching for and using chemical information; and on communicating data in poster and platform presentations.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 180 with a minimum grade of A or CHEM 199 with a minimum grade of A or PHYSICS 195 with a minimum grade of A or EARTHSS 199 with a minimum grade of A or CBEMS 199 with a minimum grade of A or ENGRCEE 199 with a minimum grade of A or ENGRMAE 199 with a minimum grade of A or BIO SCI 199 with a minimum grade of A or PUBHLTH 199 with a minimum grade of A. Consent of the instructor is also accepted. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Honors Research in Chemistry
description: Undergraduate honors research in Chemistry. A student time commitment of 10-15 hours per week is required.

title: Honors Research in Chemistry
description: Undergraduate honors research in Chemistry. A student time commitment of 10-15 hours per week is required.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM H180A

title: Honors Research in Chemistry
description: Undergraduate honors research in Chemistry. A student time committment of 10-15 hours per week is required.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM H180B

title: Honors Seminar in Chemistry
description: Students will receive guidance in the preparation of oral and written research presentations. A written thesis will be prepared and a formal research seminar will be presented.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM H180A and CHEM H180B . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Tutoring in Chemistry
description: Enrollment limited to participants in the Chemistry Peer Tutoring Program.

title: Research Methods
description: Explores tools of inquiry for developing and implementing science research projects. Students undertake independent projects requiring data collection, analysis, and modeling, and the organization and presentation of results. Additional topics include ethical issues and role of scientific literature.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 14 or PHY SCI 5

title: Professional Internship
description: Internship program that provides students with opportunity to develop professional skills necessary for competitive placement in their chosen chemical-inspired industry. Students gain new and field-specific skills outside the classroom while participating in a supervised internship.
prerequisites_raw: Enrollment requires completion of an application form

title: Independent Study in Chemistry
description: Independent research with Chemistry faculty. Student time commitment of three to four hours per week per unit is expected, and a written report on the independent study is required at the end of each quarter of enrollment.

title: Conduct of Research
description: Introduces new graduate students to ethical conduct of scientific research, mentoring, and current research in the Department of Chemistry.

title: Organic Reaction Mechanisms I
description: Advanced treatment of basic mechanistic principles of modern organic chemistry. Topics include molecular orbital theory, orbital symmetry control of organic reactions, aromaticity, carbonium ion chemistry, free radical chemistry, the chemistry of carbenes and carbanions, photochemistry, electrophilic substitutions, aromatic chemistry.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 132A and CHEM 132B and CHEM 132C

title: Organic Reaction Mechanisms II
description: Topics include more in-depth treatment of mechanistic concepts, kinetics, conformational analysis, computational methods, stereoelectronics, and both solution and enzymatic catalysis.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 201 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Organic Spectroscopy
description: Modern methods used in structure determination of organic molecules. Topics include mass spectrometry; ultraviolet, chiroptical, infrared, and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.
prerequisites_raw: ( CHEM 51A and CHEM 51B and CHEM 51C ) or (CHEM H52A and CHEM H52B and CHEM H52C)

title: Organic Synthesis I
description: Fundamentals of modern synthetic organic chemistry is developed. Major emphasis is on carbon-carbon bond forming methodology. Topics include carbonyl annelations, cycloadditions, sigmatropic rearrangements, and organometallic methods.

title: Organic Synthesis II
description: Fundamentals of modern synthetic organic chemistry will be developed. Major emphasis this quarter is on natural product total synthesis and retrosynthetic (antithetic) analysis.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 204 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Advanced Data Acquisition and Analysis
description: Introduces students to a variety of practical laboratory techniques, including lock-in, boxcar, coincidence counting, noise filtering, PID control, properties of common transducers, computer interfacing to instruments, vacuum technology, laboratory safety, basic mechanical design, and shop skills. Materials Fee

title: Applied Physical Chemistry
description: Introduction to fundamental concepts in molecular structure and reactivity: theory of bonding, valence and molecular orbitals; structure and reactivity in inorganic chemistry; elements in molecular group theory; nomenclature in organic chemistry; and survey of macromolecules.

title: Math Methods
description: Applications of mathematics to physical and chemical problems. Calculus of special functions, complex variables and vectors; linear vector spaces and eigenvalue problems. Differential equations.

title: Chemical Kinetics
description: Surveys gas phase and organic reaction mechanisms and their relationship to kinetic rate laws; treats the basic theory of elementary reaction rates. A brief presentation of modern cross-sectional kinetics is included.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 132A and CHEM 132B and CHEM 132C

title: Inorganic Chemistry I
description: Principles of modern inorganic chemistry with applications to chemical systems of current interest. Inorganic phenomena are organized into general patterns which rationalize observed structures, stabilities, and physical properties.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 107 and CHEM 132A and CHEM 132B and CHEM 132C

title: Organometallic Chemistry
description: Synthesis and reactivity of organometallic complexes with an emphasis on mechanisms. Topics include bonding and fluxional properties; metal-carbon single and multiple bonds; metal š-complexes. Applications to homogenous catalysis and organic synthesis are incorporated throughout the course.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 107 or CHEM 215 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Physical Inorganic Chemistry
description: General principles of the spectroscopy and magnetism of inorganic compounds. Characterization of inorganic complexes by infrared, near-infrared, visible, ultraviolet, NMR, EPR, EXAFS, and Mossbauer spectroscopies. Some necessary group theory developed.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 215 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Metallobiochemistry
description: A review of the biochemistry of metallic elements emphasizing: methods for studying metals in biological systems; the chemical basis for nature's exploitation of specific elements; structures of active sites; mechanisms; solid-state structures and devices; metals in medicine.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 131C (may be taken concurrently) or CHEM 132C (may be taken concurrently)

title: Chemical and Structural Biology
description: A survey of the organic chemistry underlying biological function. Introduction to chemical genetics, receptor-ligand interactions, small molecule agonists and antagonists, combinatorial synthesis, high throughput assays, molecular evolution, protein and small molecule design.

title: Advanced Chemical Biology
description: Modern topics in chemical biology, with an emphasis on application of principles from organic chemistry to biological research and biotechnology. Topics include methods to generate, identify, and manipulate major classes of biomolecules including nucleic acids, carbohydrates, lipids, and secondary metabolites.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 219 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Fundamentals of Molecular Biophysics
description: An overview of the principles and concepts in molecular biophysics. Topics covered include energy and entropy in biology, non-equilibrium reaction kinetics, random walks and molecular diffusion, molecular forces in biology.
prerequisites_raw: Undergraduate courses in physical chemistry and biochemistry

title: Biological Macromolecules
description: Introduction to nucleic acid and protein structure, dynamics, and function. Topics include analytical methods, molecular evolution, folding, and catalysis.

title: Polymer Chemistry: Synthesis and Characterization of Polymers
description: Structure of synthetic and natural polymers. Survey of modern polymer synthetic methods. Molecular weight and molecular weight distribution. Chain conformation and stereochemistry. Introduction to polymer characterization, chain models, and solution behavior.
prerequisites_raw: Undergraduate courses in organic and physical chemistry

title: Electromagnetism
description: Maxwell’s equations, electrodynamics, electromagnetic waves and radiation, wave propagation in media, interference and quantum optics, coherent and incoherent radiation, with practical applications in interferometry, lasers, waveguides, and optical instrumentation.

title: Mathematical Methods for the Physical Sciences
description: Mathematical and numerical analysis using Mathematica and C programming, as applied to problems in physical science.

title: Classical Mechanics and Electromagnetic Theory
description: Fundamentals of classical mechanics and electromagnetic theory are developed with specific application to molecular systems. Newtonian, Lagrangian, and Hamiltonian mechanics are developed. Boundary value problems in electrostatics are investigated. Multipole expansion and macroscopic media are discussed from a molecular viewpoint.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 132A and CHEM 132B and CHEM 132C

title: Fundamentals of Quantum Mechanics
description: The postulates of quantum mechanics are discussed and applied to a variety of model problems.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 131A and CHEM 131B and CHEM 131C

title: Applications of Quantum Mechanics
description: Approximate methods for solving atomic and molecular structure problems are developed, and the application of quantum mechanics to spectroscopy is introduced.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 231A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Molecular Spectroscopy
description: Theory and techniques of spectroscopy as used for the study of molecular and condensed phase properties. Coherent time domain spectroscopies are covered.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 231B with a minimum grade of B-

title: Thermodynamics and Introduction to Statistical Mechanics
description: A detailed discussion from an advanced point of view of the principles of classical thermodynamics. The fundamentals of statistical mechanics. Topics include an introduction to ensemble theory, Boltzmann statistics, classical statistical mechanics, and the statistical mechanics of ideal gas systems.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 131A and CHEM 131B and CHEM 131C

title: Advanced Topics in Statistical Mechanics
description: Continued discussion of the principles of statistical mechanics. Applications to topics of chemical interest including imperfect gases, liquids, solutions, and crystals. Modern techniques such as the use of autocorrelation function methods.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 232A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Non-Equilibrium Statistical Mechanics
description: Phenomenology of material processes, including: kinetic theories of transport and continuum, linear response theory, critical phenomena of phase transition, self-assembly, and nucleation.

title: Nuclear and Radiochemistry
description: Advanced treatment of nuclear structure, nuclear reactions, and radioactive-decay processes. Introduction to nuclear activation analysis, isotope effects, radiation chemistry, hot-atom chemistry, nuclear age-dating methods, nuclear reactors, and nuclear power.

title: Mathematical Methods in Chemistry
description: Survey of essential math methods in chemistry. Topics may include series and limits, complex analysis, Fourier and Laplace transforms, linear algebra and operators (theory and algorithms), differential equations, and probability concepts for stochastic processes.

title: Special Topics in Density Functional Theory
description: Advanced topics in density functional theory.
prerequisites_raw: One year of graduate quantum mechanics, or the equivalent

title: Machine Learning in Chemistry
description: Introductory course in machine learning, accessible to any graduate student in chemistry. Covers the basics of theory and practice of machine learning in modern chemistry. No coding or previous experience required.
prerequisites_raw: Must be familiar with standard computer operation

title: Current Issues Related to Air Quality, Climate, and Energy
description: Current issues related to the atmosphere, climate, and air quality in the context of energy conversion and sustainability. Topics include transportation systems; building design; impacts on humans and ecosystems; modeling and meteorology; economics; and application to public policies.
prerequisites_raw: ENGRMAE 261 with a minimum grade of B- or CHEM 245 with a minimum grade of B- or EARTHSS 240 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Advanced Instrumental Analysis
description: Theory and applications of modern advanced instrumental methods of analysis. Includes data acquisition, storage, retrieval, and analysis; Fourier transform methods; vacuum technologies; magnetic sector; quadrupole and ion trap mass spectrometry; surface science spectroscopic methods; lasers and optics.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 152 with a minimum grade of B and CHEM 132C with a minimum grade of B

title: Detection and Measurement of Radiation
description: Basic principles of detection and measurement of ionizing radiation; both theory and practical aspects of measurement techniques for alpha, beta, gamma, and neutron radiation, properties of different detector materials, electronics and data treatments, and analysis.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 233 with a minimum grade of B- or CBE 276 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Gas-Phase Atmospheric Chemistry
description: Sources, chemistry, sinks, and measurements of key atmospheric gaseous species. Chemistry of photochemical oxidant formation, transformation of key inorganic and organic trace gases, and stratospheric ozone cycling. Applications of atmospheric chemistry models to control strategies.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 132A and CHEM 132B and CHEM 132C

title: Multi-Phase Atmospheric Chemistry
description: Chemical and physical processes leading to the production, aging, and removal of atmospheric particles. Multi-phase processes involving gases, particles, water droplets, and environmental surfaces. Approaches for modeling these processes with applications to control strategies.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 245A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Special Topics in Atmospheric Chemistry
description: The subjects covered vary from year to year.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 245B with a minimum grade of B-

title: Separations and Chromatography
description: Introduction to modern separation techniques such as gas chromatography, high-performance liquid chromatography, supercritical fluid chromatography, capillary electrophoresis, and field flow fractionation. Applications of these separation strategies are discussed.
